title: Weight-Space Programming for Targeted Repair of Robot Foundation Models
read_level: full (PDF v1, 8 pages incl. appendix figures; no HTML available; figure contents not read beyond captions)
metadata_mismatch: Title differs: arXiv metadata title is 'Sparks of Weight-Space Programming for Robot Foundation Models'; PDF title is 'Weight-Space Programming for Targeted Repair of Robot Foundation Models'. Authors match.
why_wsp: Claude Opus 5.5 with tool access runs a Pi0.5 policy in RoboTwin simulation, inspects action-expert activations, finds near-silent neurons and rewrites their connections to inject task-specific corrective movements, testing each edit in simulation, with no gradient updates.
facets: application domain: robot foundation models / vision-language-action policies
domain: robot manipulation (bimanual UR5 in RoboTwin 2.0 simulation)
target: Pi0.5 VLA policy (3.35B parameters), action expert; plus a task-fine-tuned Pi0.5 checkpoint for place_mixed_objects_basket
interface: code/tensor tools (start/stop policy server, run tasks, inspect actions and neuron activity, edit weights, test in simulation)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (edit tried on initial scenes, revised, confirmed on validation scenes, locked, then tested on new scenes)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "The fixes change only about 6,000 of the model's 3.35 billion parameters"; "roughly 0.0002% of the model"; each fix rewrites connections to two near-silent neurons, one per arm.

headline_results.quote: On the hammer task, success rose from 56.5% to 70.5% across 200 new scenes: the edit fixed 41 scenes but broke 13.
On the bell task, success rose from 87.3% to 96.7% across 300 new scenes: 29 scenes were fixed and 1 was broken.
success rose from 67.7% to 84.4% across 505 new scenes: the edit fixed 121 scenes and broke 37.
hovering failures rose from 4 to 19, while successes fell from 91 to 64.
Random edits of the same size made no consistent difference.
success went from 38% to 41% on 200 new scenes, a difference that is not statistically significant. The turn_switch edits likewise showed no significant improvement
a survey of all 73,728 neurons in the module's action expert found only six that were essentially never active on the tasks checked, all in its final layer.
headline_results.where: Target Failure Modes and Edit Procedure

cost.quote: The hammer task, for instance, took four iterations.
cost.where: Target Failure Modes and Edit Procedure (no token, time or $ figures reported)

baselines_and_controls: Unedited policy on identical seeded scenes; random edits of the same size; sign-reversed edits; task-fine-tuned (30k-step full fine-tune) checkpoint as starting point for basket task. Pass mark set in advance.
runs_and_variance: single run / not reported (fixed/broken scene counts given; significance claimed only for move_can_pot as 'not statistically significant')
robustness_of_edits: Held-out new scenes with varied object, basket, texture, lighting, background; edit on top of a fine-tuned checkpoint. Not tested on real robots, under further fine-tuning or quantization.
limitations_stated: Did not solve every failure (2 of 5 tasks failed); works best when the failure situation is recognizable and a simple correction suffices; WSP for robot models at a very early stage.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 Sparks of Weight-Space Programming blog [1]
Stranghöner et al. Repairing Robot Policies with WSP (blog) [2]
Gong et al. Opus-5.5 edits Pi0.5 (blog) [4]
notes_for_survey: Short report (Siemens Research) writing corrective movements into near-silent final-layer action-expert neurons of Pi0.5; 3 of 5 targeted failures improved on held-out scenes, including on a fully fine-tuned checkpoint, with random and sign-reversed controls. No cost or variance figures.
